findings.title: Lambda-CGD noise stream is unrooted: fold_in(key, step) collides with the caller's documented key space (missed by fix #728)
findings.claim: Commit 6f6d132a (fix(random)!: namespace mechanism RNG stream roots, #728) established the repo-wide invariant that every mechanism folds a unique string tag into the key it is given before deriving per-step keys ('every stream root Opaque derives for itself is a namespaced string' — noise_allocation.py:25-38; docs/reference/rng.md tag table), and applied it to DP-SGD Gaussian (GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD, _gaussian.py:71), MF dense+streaming (MF_GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD, _engine.py:37,167,395), second-moment, adaptive clipping, and auditing. Lambda-CGD's PRNG-replay noise was missed: _lambda_cgd.py:280 'current_key = rng_fold_in(st._rng_key, step)' and :292 'prev_key = rng_fold_in(st._rng_key, step - 1)' derive privacy-noise generators directly on the caller's integer fold path. Since split(key, n) is defined as fold_in(key, i) (random/_engine.py:127) and the docs explicitly assign integer folds to the caller ('Integers are the caller's... every key split hands back'; rng.md recommends 'noise_key = fold_in(base, step)' and the split loop pattern), any caller that reuses the base key it gave lambda-CGD for an ordinary integer derivation obtains byte-identical torch.Generator streams to the mechanism's privacy noise. The public path is unguarded end to end: mf_gaussian_noise(strategy=lambda_cgd_strategy(...), key=user_key) -> _make_raw_mf_noise (_mf_gaussian_noise.py:131-139, 231-233, no root fold) -> LambdaCgdStrategy.raw_noise_factory (_lambda_cgd.py:152-169) -> fold_in(user_key, step). BiSR, the only other strategy with raw_noise_factory, routes through the rooted _matrix_factorization_noise (_bisr.py:131), so lambda-CGD is the sole surviving instance of the exact defect pattern #728 fixed. The guard test test_stream_root_namespacing.py cannot catch it because it only checks enumerated string constants, and lambda-CGD has none.
findings.failure_scenario: User writes the documented pattern: base = key(42); passes base to mf_gaussian_noise(strategy=lambda_cgd_strategy(...), key=base) and elsewhere derives step_k via split(base) or fold_in(base, step) for their own generator_from_key draws (dropout, data augmentation, a second mechanism, a logged/released random quantity). Reproduced live: with k = key(42), torch.randn(5, generator=generator_from_key(split(k, 2)[0])) is torch.equal to the lambda-CGD step-0 privacy noise (both [0.9301, 0.2699, 0.5048, -1.2086, -0.0477]). If the colliding stream is observable (released values, deterministic replay of user-side randomness), the DP noise is exactly predictable and the effective epsilon is unbounded, with no warning, error, or accounting signal. Restarting a fresh lambda-CGD mechanism with the same key also byte-replays the previous run's noise (correlated releases the fixed-horizon MF accounting does not model).
evidence: packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_lambda_cgd.py:280 'current_key = rng_fold_in(st._rng_key, step)' and :292 'prev_key = rng_fold_in(st._rng_key, step - 1)' — no string root; contrast _engine.py:395-397 streaming path 'step_key = rng_fold_in(st._rng_key, MF_GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD, "mf_gaussian_column", step)'.

packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/random/_engine.py:118-127: split(key, n) == fold_in(key, i) for i in range(n); fold_in docstring :71-83 'Integers are the caller's ... Skipping the string root is the failure this convention exists to prevent'.
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/noise_allocation.py:27-38: 'Integers belong to the caller ...; every stream root Opaque derives for itself is a namespaced string.'
docs/reference/rng.md:206-228: tag table omits lambda-CGD (it has no tag) and recommends caller patterns 'noise_key = fold_in(base, step)', 'fold_in(base, step, rank)'.

Live repro (uv run python on this tree): _make_lambda_cgd_noise(key=key(42)) step-0 output on zero grads is torch.equal to torch.randn(5, generator=generator_from_key(split(key(42), 2)[0])) — BYTE-IDENTICAL: True.

packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_mf_gaussian_noise.py:114-139 and :231-233 pass the user key verbatim to raw_noise_factory; packages/opaque-engine/tests/rng/test_stream_root_namespacing.py:26-63 enumerates only constant tags, so lambda-CGD is invisible to the guard test.
findings.fix_sketch: Root the stream: LAMBDA_CGD_STREAM_FOLD = "opaque.dpftrl.lambda_cgd" in _lambda_cgd.py; derive current_key = rng_fold_in(st._rng_key, LAMBDA_CGD_STREAM_FOLD, step) and prev_key = rng_fold_in(st._rng_key, LAMBDA_CGD_STREAM_FOLD, step - 1). This is a breaking noise-stream change (same class as #728, which was already shipped as '!'). Add the tag to docs/reference/rng.md and to _dpftrl_roots() in test_stream_root_namespacing.py; add a domain-separation test that two mechanisms (lambda-CGD + anything) sharing a base key draw non-identical noise, mirroring test_domain_separation.py in opaque-dpsgd.

findings.title: Samplers seed numpy RNG from the raw key with no domain separation (same defect class as #728, sibling surface)
findings.claim: The samplers consume the caller's key without any mechanism root: PoissonSampler does 'self.generator = np.random.default_rng(key.seed)' (_poisson.py:108), balls-in-bins does 'generator = np.random.default_rng(key.seed)' (_balls_in_bins.py:103), and random allocation does 'rng = np.random.default_rng(fold_in(self._key, epoch).seed)' (_random_allocation.py:125) — a bare integer fold on the caller's path. Under the convention #728 shipped ('a mechanism that draws randomness folds one unique string tag into the key it was given', rng.md:208-210), sampling is a randomness-drawing mechanism whose stream should be namespaced: two different samplers built from the same key draw identical PCG64 streams, and random-allocation's epoch stream is byte-identical to any caller-side np.random.default_rng(fold_in(key, epoch).seed). Sampling randomness is amplification-relevant, so stream reuse is not merely a reproducibility nit. Mitigating factors keep this low: the trainer derives the sampler key from data_seed/seed with its own string fold on the restart path (_dp_trainer.py:3688-3703), only one sampler is built per run, and the torch-side noise streams are blake2b-separated from key.seed, so no in-repo default collides.
findings.failure_scenario: A manual-loop user holds one master key and passes it to both a Poisson sampler and a balls-in-bins sampler (e.g. comparing samplers, or train + canary-insertion sampling): both consume np.random.default_rng(key.seed) and draw the identical stream, so the two 'independent' sampling processes are perfectly correlated — participation patterns coincide and any analysis multiplying their probabilities (or treating one as fresh randomness) is wrong. Similarly, a caller that publishes anything derived from default_rng(fold_in(key, epoch).seed) has published the random-allocation assignment stream, voiding the allocation's secrecy assumption. Silent in all cases.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_random_allocation.py:125 'rng = np.random.default_rng(fold_in(self._key, epoch).seed)' — integer-only fold on the caller's path.
docs/reference/rng.md:208-210 states every mechanism roots itself with a unique string tag; the tag table (rng.md:214-222) lists no sampler tags.

Trainer wiring is safe by construction, not by the samplers: _dp_trainer.py:3688 'sampler_key = key(a.data_seed if a.data_seed is not None else a.seed)' with a string fold only on the ignore_data_skip restart path (:3693-3697).
findings.fix_sketch: Give each sampler a namespaced root before seeding numpy: e.g. default_rng(fold_in(key, "opaque.dpsgd.poisson").seed), default_rng(fold_in(key, "opaque.dpftrl.balls_in_bins").seed), and fold_in(self._key, "opaque.dpsgd.random_allocation", epoch) — preserving state-dict compatibility via the stored original key. Register the tags in rng.md and the namespacing test. Note this changes sampling streams (breaking, like #728).

findings.title: _compile_with_fullgraph_fallback catches every Exception on first call, masking non-compile failures as compile fallbacks
findings.claim: The compiled DP grad transform wrapper's first-call handler is 'except Exception as e' (_dp_trainer.py:213): ANY exception raised during the first execution of the fullgraph=True compiled grad_fn — an MPS/CUDA OOM, a data-dependent runtime error (bad labels, non-finite loss check), a bug in a user loss closure — is logged as 'torch.compile fullgraph=True failed (...); falling back to fullgraph=False' and the entire step is silently re-executed under a fullgraph=False recompile (:220-221). Genuine errors will usually re-raise from the fallback so nothing is permanently swallowed, but the first failure's identity is misattributed to torch.compile, the step body runs twice (doubling peak-memory pressure exactly when the first failure was an OOM), and a first-call-only transient error (e.g. an inductor-numerics-triggered assert that eager does not hit) is permanently absorbed with only a misleading compile warning. grad_fn is functional (state passed and returned), so the double execution itself does not corrupt clipping or noise state.
findings.failure_scenario: torch_compile=True on MPS; the first training step OOMs inside the compiled vmap(grad)+clip transform. The user sees 'torch.compile fullgraph=True failed (OutOfMemoryError: ...)' — pointing them at compile flags — while the wrapper immediately re-runs the full forward/backward under a fresh fullgraph=False compilation on an already-exhausted allocator. Debugging is misdirected and the retry can push a borderline configuration over the memory cliff.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:211-221: 'try: return full(*args, **kwargs) / except Exception as e: log.warning("torch.compile fullgraph=True failed (%s: %s); falling back...") / fallback = torch.compile(fn, ..., fullgraph=False) / return fallback(*args, **kwargs)'.

The docstring (:192-201) motivates the catch as a graph-break fallback, but graph-break failures under fullgraph=True surface as torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported / BackendCompilerFailed — a narrow set, not Exception.
Interaction with OOM handling: the trainer's collective OOM logic (:2050-2084) only sees the exception the wrapper re-raises from the fallback path, after a second full execution.
findings.fix_sketch: Narrow the catch to compile-classified failures (torch._dynamo.exc.TorchDynamoException / BackendCompilerFailed / Unsupported), and explicitly re-raise torch.OutOfMemoryError without retry so the trainer's OOM path sees it first-hand. Keep the lazy fallback semantics otherwise.

findings.title: StepPerf.memory_peak_gb on MPS is the run-wide reserved high-water, not the per-step peak its docstring claims
findings.claim: On MPS, get_memory_stats reports peak_gb = torch.mps.driver_allocated_memory() (the driver's monotonic reserved high-water, _memory.py:162-171) and step_perf deliberately never resets it per step (peak_memory_trackable is False for MPS — _capabilities.py:124-129, gate at _memory.py:414). The internal comments document this accurately, but the user-facing StepPerf dataclass docstring says 'memory_peak_gb: Peak GPU memory during the step' (_memory.py:275) and MemoryStats marks the value exact_peak=True (:174). So per-step logs on MPS (StepPerf.to_dict -> 'memory_peak_gb', wandb examples in the module docstring) show a monotonically non-decreasing run-cumulative figure labeled as a per-step peak, and per-step regressions/comparisons on MPS are meaningless while looking precise. CUDA behavior (true per-step peak, reset each step) diverges silently from MPS behavior under the same field name.
findings.failure_scenario: A user profiling a DP step on Apple Silicon logs sp.perf.to_dict(prefix='train/') per step and concludes step 500's 'memory_peak_gb' equals step 500's peak usage; in reality it is the maximum reservation ever reached since process start (e.g. inflated by an earlier eval or the first uncompiled step), so a memory optimization that actually halves step usage shows no change in the logged per-step 'peak'.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/profiling/_memory.py:162-178: MPS branch sets peak_gb=reserved (driver_allocated_memory) with exact_peak=True.

packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/profiling/_memory.py:410-415: 'if track_memory and device_capabilities(device).peak_memory_trackable: reset_peak_memory(device)' — never true on MPS (_capabilities.py:124-129 'return device_type == "cuda"').
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/profiling/_memory.py:273-279: StepPerf docstring 'memory_peak_gb: Peak GPU memory during the step.' — wrong for MPS.
findings.fix_sketch: Either document the MPS semantics on StepPerf.memory_peak_gb itself (run high-water on MPS, per-step peak on CUDA) and surface a boolean like peak_is_per_step in to_dict, or approximate a per-step figure on MPS as max(current_allocated at marks) while keeping the high-water separately.

clean_areas: Checked the MPS float32 squared-norm accumulator path added by #598 (_pytree.py:_sq_accum_dtype returns fp32 when any leaf is on MPS, fp64 elsewhere) by deriving the rounding budget and by brute force: monkeypatched _sq_accum_dtype to fp32 (simulating MPS) and stress-tested clip_pytree and auto_scale_pytree over 300 adversarial cases (fp32/bf16/fp16 leaves up to 5e5 elements, norms within 1e-7..10x of C, subnormal leaves, a 4M-element bf16 leaf, C in {1e-6, 1, 12345.678}); the stored-value bound norm(output) <= C held with zero excess in every case. The guard math (_guard_scale relative = 1 - 2*(u_store + norm_roundoff), _norm_roundoff counting squaring + worst-case sequential additions of the blocked reduction + cross-leaf additions, halved through sqrt) is conservative for any summation order, so inductor reassociation under torch.compile cannot break it (worst-case sequential rounding upper-bounds every association order).

Checked DP-SGD Gaussian noise RNG device-independence end to end: generator_from_key (random/_engine.py:130-133) always constructs a CPU torch.Generator; _gaussian._sample draws uniforms with torch.rand(shape, dtype=compute_dtype, generator=cpu_gen) and only then moves to the gradient device, so the random stream is identical on CPU/CUDA/MPS with only on-device erfinv ULP differences; tests/noise/test_device_parity.py locks CPU-vs-MPS and CPU-vs-CUDA at atol 1e-4 with a non-vacuous different-key guard. Noise is computed in fp32 regardless of bf16 gradients and only the noised sum is cast back to the input dtype (post-processing).

Checked the MF noise CPU-generator fallback on accelerators: _engine.py _randn_on_device and _gaussian_linear_combination catch RuntimeError matching 'device type for generator' and resample on CPU + .to(device); verified the exact substring exists in the installed torch 2.13 ATen check_generator (include/ATen/core/Generator.h:155 and libtorch_cpu.so strings), which is the generic path MPS/CUDA generator-mismatch errors go through, and that torch>=2.9 is the engine's floor (opaque-engine/pyproject.toml). CPU-vs-accelerator draws are identical because the CPU branch and the fallback consume the same generator with the same dtype.

Checked #518's MF Gaussian column-reuse rework plus #728's rooting in the dense and streaming MF engines: dense per-(column, leaf) keys fold_in(key, MF_GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD, 'mf_gaussian_column', idx, leaf_index) are reused across rows (correct correlated-noise structure) and cannot collide with the streaming per-step keys (different fold depths under the same root); second-moment streams are separated by SECOND_MOMENT_FIRST/SECOND string folds (_second_moment.py:92,101). Ran the rng namespacing, clipping-numerics, and device-capabilities test files on this tree: 85 passed.

Checked lambda-CGD PRNG replay determinism across devices and resume (separately from the rooting defect reported above): z_prev is regenerated from a fresh CPU generator with the same derived key, _iid_normal_noise draws leaves in deterministic tree order, state carries only _step_counter + _rng_key, so replay is bit-exact across CPU/CUDA/MPS and across checkpoint restore.

Checked bf16/mixed-precision gating in the trainer: bf16 is the only AMP mode (fp16 training rejected, _training_arguments.py:726-751); MPS bf16 is admitted only when the empirical _probe_bf16('mps') allocate-and-run probe passes, and probe failures of any kind return False -> hard ValueError (fail-closed). Autocast wraps only the outer grad_fn call (_dp_trainer.py:2053-2060) — noise_fn runs outside autocast, and autocast cannot downcast the clip-norm reductions (pointwise ops and explicit-dtype sums are not autocast-eligible). The MPS bf16 SDPA-under-vmap bug is handled by an empirical probe (sdpa_autocast_under_vmap_broken) that switches the model to eager attention or warns and lets the step fail loudly — no silent wrong-dtype path.

Checked float64-on-MPS failure modes: clipping uses the fp32 accumulator with a widened guard (above); compute_dtype=torch.float64 passed to gaussian_noise or mf_gaussian_noise on MPS fails loudly (f64 tensors cannot be moved to MPS and the raised error does not match the generator-fallback substring, so it re-raises); MF strategy coefficient math (Toeplitz/band/streaming matrices) is computed in float64 on CPU and only downcast to the state dtype at apply time (_toeplitz.py:248-250); PLD accounting is torch-free Rust f64 and unaffected by the compute device.

Checked that no DP randomness can fall back to global/device RNG: all _iid_normal_noise call sites pass explicit generators; adaptive-clipping quantile noise uses generator_from_key with rooted folds (touched by #728); the repo contains no PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK usage, so no silent MPS->CPU op fallback is enabled by the library.

Checked torch.compile integration boundaries: only the vmap(grad)+clip transform is compiled (_grad_compiler/_create_grad_fn); noise_fn, the sampler, and the accountant run eager, so inductor cannot re-lower noise sampling; compile on a device without a backend logs a warning and runs eager rather than mis-targeting; torch_compile + auto_find_microbatch_size is rejected at argument validation. grad_fn is functional so the fallback wrapper's re-execution cannot double-advance clip or noise state.

Checked the trainer's MPS device plumbing: unsupported device types are rejected at construction (_dp_trainer.py:520-527); pin_memory is CUDA-only (no MPS warning spam); empty_cache paths use torch.mps.empty_cache; OOM retry classification uses isinstance(err, torch.OutOfMemoryError), which MPS's allocator raises on torch>=2.9 (the engine's floor); reproducible seeding seeds torch.mps.manual_seed alongside CUDA (random/_helpers.py:99-103) while DP noise never touches those global RNGs.

Verified there was no separate 'backend-split' refactor in the remediation window: git log 79c916e3..4b13d82 contains no backend-split commit; PR #267 (ef88bdff, the MPS stabilization) predates the pre-remediation tip, and the delta commits touching this surface are #598 (clipping numerics), #728 (RNG roots), #518 (MF column reuse), #715/#681 (fp16 loss-scaler lane), all inspected above.
